name: Battle of Tarawa

phases.title: The warships bombard Betio
phases.text: Warships and aircraft shelled the island for about three hours before the landing. The Marines waited in the lagoon to land on the north beaches, while the defenders sat in their pillboxes and firing pits.

phases.title: The landing is pinned down at the sea wall
phases.text: The tide was too low for the Higgins boats, and only the tracked LVTs crossed the reef. They could not clear the sea wall, so the first waves were pinned against it. Defenders from the south beaches were shifted to the north.

phases.title: By nightfall the line is half-way across
phases.text: The arrival of tanks started the line moving on Red 3 and the end of Red 2. By nightfall it was about half-way across the island, only a short distance from the main runway.

phases.title: Ryan's Orphans clear the western end
phases.text: Major Ryan gathered remnants of his company with Marines and sailors from other waves and two Sherman tanks, and took them to a more lightly defended part of Green Beach. With naval gunfire they cleared the western end of the island.

phases.title: The Marines cross the airstrip
phases.text: Machine gun posts set up in the night had cut the Marines of Red 2 and Red 3 off from each other. By noon heavy machine guns put them out of action, and by early afternoon the Marines had crossed the airstrip to the south side.

phases.title: Marines land on Bairiki
phases.text: Word came that some defenders were crossing the sandbars to Bairiki. Portions of the 6th Marines landed there, with tanks and pack artillery, to seal off the retreat path. They found a single pillbox, which aircraft set on fire.

phases.title: The 1st Battalion, 6th Marines attacks along the south coast
phases.text: The 1st Battalion, 6th Marines, formed up after landing on Green Beach, attacked at 12:30 and pressed the Japanese east along the south coast. By late afternoon it had reached the eastern end of the airfield and joined the line from Red 3.

phases.title: The Japanese counterattack is broken up
phases.text: That night the Japanese formed up for a counterattack and sent small units to infiltrate the American lines. Concentrated artillery fire broke up the assembling force, and the full assault never took place.

phases.title: The banzai charge at night
phases.text: A large banzai charge was made at 03:00 and met with some success, killing 45 Americans and wounding 128. With support from the destroyers Schroeder and Sigsbee, the Marines killed 325 Japanese attackers.

phases.title: The Marines attack both pockets
phases.text: The 3rd Battalion, 6th Marines relieved the first battalion and attacked the eastern end. The 3rd Battalion, 2nd and the 1st Battalion, 8th closed on the pocket between Red 1 and Red 2 from west and east.

phases.title: The island is declared secure
phases.text: By noon the pocket between Red 1 and Red 2 had been reduced. The 3rd Battalion, 6th Marines reached the eastern tip by 13:00, and the island was declared secure at 13:30.

note: The plan shows the whole four-day operation on Betio, not a single field. Each block stands for the Marines or defenders of a stretch of the island, so positions are rough. The accounts give no place for the warships; they are drawn offshore. The accounts do not say how the defenders were spread along the island, so the Japanese blocks are placed by the beaches and the pocket the accounts name. The Japanese pocket between Red 1 and Red 2 is drawn as the whole garrison's remnant, which the accounts do not claim.
